contentMethod: Ogden Basic English inspired: core operators plus essential BA and Scrum Master terms

sentencePatterns: Overall, the project is...
We have completed...
The next step is...
examples: Give a concise update with status, evidence, and the next action.

sentences.text: Overall, the project is on track, and we are still working toward the agreed target date.
sentences.pattern: Overall, the project is on track, and we are still working toward...
examples: Overall, the project is on track, and we are still working toward the June release.
Overall, the migration is on track, and we are still working toward the agreed cutover date.

sentences.text: We have completed the main analysis, and the key requirements are now aligned with the business team.
sentences.pattern: We have completed..., and ... are now aligned with...
examples: We have completed the SIT preparation, and the test scope is now aligned with QA.
We have completed the impact assessment, and the findings are now aligned with Finance.

sentences.text: The next step is to close the remaining open items before we move into delivery.
sentences.pattern: The next step is to... before we move into...
examples: The next step is to obtain sign-off before we move into UAT.
The next step is to confirm the data mapping before we move into development.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Give a concise project update covering status, evidence, and the next step.

sentencePatterns: Just to confirm my understanding...
Could you clarify whether...
Once we confirm..., I can...
examples: Clarify the intent before discussing a solution.

sentences.text: Just to confirm my understanding, the new rule should apply only to payments above the approval threshold.
sentences.pattern: Just to confirm my understanding, ... should apply only to...
examples: Just to confirm my understanding, this control should apply only to corporate users.
Just to confirm my understanding, the change should apply only to new instructions.

sentences.text: Could you clarify whether this is a regulatory requirement or a business preference?
sentences.pattern: Could you clarify whether this is... or...?
examples: Could you clarify whether this is needed for day one or a later phase?
Could you clarify whether this applies to all markets or only Hong Kong?

sentences.text: Once we confirm the expected outcome, I can update the acceptance criteria and share them for sign-off.
sentences.pattern: Once we confirm..., I can... and share...
examples: Once we confirm the exception flow, I can update the story and share it for review.
Once we confirm the data owner, I can update the requirement and request sign-off.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Clarify one ambiguous requirement and propose how to close it.

sentencePatterns: We have identified one potential risk that may impact...
The main concern is that...
I have already followed up with...
If there is no update by..., we may need to...
examples: State the risk, current action, and escalation point.

sentences.text: We have identified one potential risk that may impact the delivery timeline.
sentences.pattern: We have identified one potential risk that may impact...
examples: We have identified one potential risk that may impact the UAT timeline.
We have identified one potential risk that may impact the production release.

sentences.text: The main concern is that we are still waiting for input from the upstream team, and this is currently blocking the next step.
sentences.pattern: The main concern is that we are still waiting for..., and this is currently blocking...
examples: The main concern is that we are still waiting for test data, and this is currently blocking SIT.
The main concern is that we are still waiting for approval, and this is currently blocking deployment.

sentences.text: I have already followed up with them, but we have not received a confirmed date yet.
sentences.pattern: I have already followed up with..., but we have not received... yet.
examples: I have already followed up with the vendor, but we have not received the estimate yet.
I have already followed up with Operations, but we have not received sign-off yet.

sentences.text: If there is no update by tomorrow, we may need to escalate this issue and discuss a workaround with the team.
sentences.pattern: If there is no update by..., we may need to escalate... and discuss...
examples: If there is no update by Friday, we may need to escalate the dependency and discuss a workaround.
If there is no approval by noon, we may need to escalate the issue and revisit the release plan.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Give a short risk update using today’s sentence patterns.

sentencePatterns: We still have one open item on...
Can we confirm who will own...
Let’s set... as the target date...
examples: Turn discussion into clear ownership and dates.

sentences.text: We still have one open item on the interface specification, and it needs to be closed before refinement.
sentences.pattern: We still have one open item on..., and it needs to be closed before...
examples: We still have one open item on the control design, and it needs to be closed before sign-off.
We still have one open item on the test scope, and it needs to be closed before SIT.

sentences.text: Can we confirm who will own this action and coordinate with the downstream team?
sentences.pattern: Can we confirm who will own... and coordinate with...?
examples: Can we confirm who will own the data check and coordinate with Operations?
Can we confirm who will own the defect and coordinate with the vendor?

sentences.text: Let’s set Thursday as the target date and review the status in our next checkpoint.
sentences.pattern: Let’s set... as the target date and review...
examples: Let’s set 15 October as the target date and review progress next week.
Let’s set end of day as the target date and review the evidence tomorrow.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Close a meeting by assigning an owner and target date to an open item.

sentencePatterns: The overall status remains...
This week, the team...
Next week, our focus will be...
examples: Lead with the headline before supporting detail.

sentences.text: The overall status remains green, with no change to the agreed scope or timeline.
sentences.pattern: The overall status remains..., with no change to...
examples: The overall status remains amber, with no change to the release date at this stage.
The overall status remains green, with no change to the UAT plan.

sentences.text: This week, the team completed the design review and resolved the outstanding business questions.
sentences.pattern: This week, the team completed... and resolved...
examples: This week, the team completed SIT and resolved the high-priority defects.
This week, the team completed the walkthrough and resolved the data questions.

sentences.text: Next week, our focus will be finalizing the test data and preparing for UAT sign-off.
sentences.pattern: Next week, our focus will be... and...
examples: Next week, our focus will be completing development and preparing for SIT.
Next week, our focus will be closing actions and preparing for the release review.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Give a weekly status update with a headline, achievements, and next-week focus.

sentencePatterns: To keep us focused...
It sounds like we agree that...
Can I confirm that the decision is...?
examples: Guide the group from discussion to decision.

sentences.text: To keep us focused, I suggest we first agree on the business outcome and then discuss the technical approach.
sentences.pattern: To keep us focused, I suggest we first... and then...
examples: To keep us focused, I suggest we first close the scope and then discuss dates.
To keep us focused, I suggest we first review the facts and then discuss options.

sentences.text: It sounds like we agree that the manual control is acceptable for the first release.
sentences.pattern: It sounds like we agree that...
examples: It sounds like we agree that option two gives us the best trade-off.
It sounds like we agree that this item should move to the next sprint.

sentences.text: Can I confirm that the decision is to proceed with option two, subject to Security sign-off?
sentences.pattern: Can I confirm that the decision is to..., subject to...?
examples: Can I confirm that the decision is to release on Friday, subject to UAT sign-off?
Can I confirm that the decision is to retain the current process for phase one?

speakingChallenge.instruction: Facilitate a short discussion and close with a clearly stated decision.

sentencePatterns: I understand why this change is important...
Before we include it...
We can either... or...
examples: Acknowledge the need without bypassing impact assessment.

sentences.text: I understand why this change is important, especially given the impact on the operations team.
sentences.pattern: I understand why this change is important, especially given...
examples: I understand why this change is important, especially given the regulatory deadline.
I understand why this change is important, especially given the client impact.

sentences.text: Before we include it in the release, we need to assess the effort, test impact, and delivery risk.
sentences.pattern: Before we include it in..., we need to assess...
examples: Before we include it in this sprint, we need to assess the effort and dependencies.
Before we include it in UAT, we need to assess the data and control impact.

sentences.text: We can either protect the current date and move this item to phase two, or revisit the release timeline.
sentences.pattern: We can either... or...
examples: We can either reduce the scope or add capacity to the sprint.
We can either use a manual workaround or move the target date.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Respond to a late scope change and present two workable options.

sentencePatterns: I understand the urgency, but...
I would prefer to give you... rather than...
Let me align with... and I will come back with...
examples: Be responsive without making an unsupported commitment.

sentences.text: I understand the urgency, but I don’t want to commit to a date before we confirm the effort with the team.
sentences.pattern: I understand the urgency, but I don’t want to commit to... before...
examples: I understand the urgency, but I don’t want to confirm the release before we review the test results.
I understand the urgency, but I don’t want to commit to the scope before we assess the impact.

sentences.text: At this stage, I would prefer to give you a realistic timeline rather than an aggressive estimate that we may not be able to meet.
sentences.pattern: I would prefer to give you... rather than...
examples: I would prefer to give you a confirmed answer rather than an assumption we may need to change.
I would prefer to agree a realistic scope rather than overcommit the team.

sentences.text: Let me align with the development team first, and I will come back with a confirmed plan.
sentences.pattern: Let me align with... first, and I will come back with...
examples: Let me align with Compliance first, and I will come back with a confirmed position.
Let me align with the vendor first, and I will come back with a revised estimate.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Respond to an urgent date request without overcommitting the team.

sentencePatterns: I agree with the objective...
Could we test the assumption that...
Would it be worth considering...?
examples: Challenge the proposed method while supporting the goal.

sentences.text: I agree with the objective, but I’m not yet convinced that this requirement is the simplest way to achieve it.
sentences.pattern: I agree with the objective, but I’m not yet convinced that...
examples: I agree with the objective, but I’m not yet convinced that a new workflow is necessary.
I agree with the objective, but I’m not yet convinced that this belongs in phase one.

sentences.text: Could we test the assumption that every user needs the same level of access?
sentences.pattern: Could we test the assumption that...?
examples: Could we test the assumption that all records need manual review?
Could we test the assumption that this data must be available in real time?

sentences.text: Would it be worth considering a rule-based exception instead of changing the full process?
sentences.pattern: Would it be worth considering... instead of...?
examples: Would it be worth considering a configuration change instead of custom development?
Would it be worth considering a pilot instead of a full rollout?

speakingChallenge.instruction: Challenge a proposed requirement while keeping the conversation constructive.

sentencePatterns: I can see the value in...
The constraint we have is...
If this becomes the priority...
examples: Make the trade-off explicit and let stakeholders choose.

sentences.text: I can see the value in adding this feature, and it would improve the user experience.
sentences.pattern: I can see the value in..., and it would...
examples: I can see the value in automating this check, and it would reduce manual effort.
I can see the value in bringing this forward, and it would help Operations.

sentences.text: The constraint we have is limited capacity in the current sprint.
sentences.pattern: The constraint we have is...
examples: The constraint we have is the fixed regulatory date.
The constraint we have is the dependency on the vendor release.

sentences.text: If this becomes the priority, we will need to agree which existing item can move out.
sentences.pattern: If this becomes the priority, we will need to agree...
examples: If this becomes the priority, we will need to agree which control can follow later.
If this becomes the priority, we will need to agree how to protect the timeline.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Push back on a new request by explaining the trade-off and asking for a priority decision.

sentencePatterns: The system has to give us...
Can we see whether... is possible...?
Let us make the choice on...
Before I get..., I make a comparison of...
examples: Use simple operator phrases to connect a design choice to business needs.

sentences.text: From the business side, the system has to give us a clear record of every change.
sentences.pattern: From the business side, the system has to give us...
examples: The report has to give us a clear record of every approval.
The process has to give Operations a clear view of every error.

sentences.text: Can we see whether this design is possible with the system we have now?
sentences.pattern: Can we see whether... is possible with... we have now?
examples: Can we see whether this API is possible with the platform we have now?
Can we see whether this control is possible without a system change?

sentences.text: Let us make the choice on cost, time, and support needs.
sentences.pattern: Let us make the choice on..., ..., and...
examples: Let us make the choice on business value, risk, and delivery time.
Let us make the choice on system fit, cost, and long-term support.

sentences.text: Before I get a new phone, I make a comparison of price, size, and battery life.
sentences.pattern: Before I get..., I make a comparison of...
examples: Before I get a new bag, I make a comparison of price and quality.
Before I get a new camera, I make a comparison of size and weight.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Give three simple points for a technical choice, then use the same comparison pattern for a life choice.

sentencePatterns: Please send... in the API response.
We need to have a clear rule for...
Which team will take control when...?
When I send..., I keep... until...
examples: Use send, have, take, and keep for a clear API discussion.

sentences.text: Please send the payment status, error code, and last update time in the API response.
sentences.pattern: Please send..., ..., and... in the API response.
examples: Please send the request ID and result in the API response.
Please send the account status and update time in the API response.

sentences.text: We need to have a clear rule for a timeout or the same request coming in twice.
sentences.pattern: We need to have a clear rule for...
examples: We need to have a clear rule for an empty response.
We need to have a clear rule for a request coming in after cut-off.

sentences.text: Which team will take control when the upstream API is down in production?
sentences.pattern: Which team will take control when...?
examples: Which team will take control when the payment API is slow?
Which team will take control when the message does not get to the downstream system?

sentences.text: When I send money to a friend, I keep the receipt until the payment is complete.
sentences.pattern: When I send..., I keep... until...
examples: When I send a parcel, I keep the receipt until it gets there.
When I send a form, I keep a copy until I get an answer.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Give an API update with information, error rules, and ownership, then add one everyday send-and-keep example.

sentencePatterns: We can see... without...
This error may have an effect on...
Let us make a check of... before...
I keep... the same in...
examples: Keep facts, effects, and the next check separate.

sentences.text: We can see some customer records without a source-system ID.
sentences.pattern: We can see some... without...
examples: We can see some payments without a booking date.
We can see some accounts without a product code.

sentences.text: This error may have an effect on payment matching and the control report.
sentences.pattern: This error may have an effect on... and...
examples: This error may have an effect on customer letters and monthly reports.
This error may have an effect on account matching and sign-off.

sentences.text: Let us make a check of the source data and the data mapping before we put in a fix.
sentences.pattern: Let us make a check of... before we put in...
examples: Let us make a check of the file and the API response before we put in a fix.
Let us make a check of the test data before we put in a new rule.

sentences.text: I keep my home address the same in my bank and delivery apps.
sentences.pattern: I keep... the same in... and...
examples: I keep my phone number the same in my bank and store accounts.
I keep my name the same on my ticket and ID.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Say what you see, give the business effect, and make a simple check plan, then add one life data example.

sentencePatterns: The migration will take in...
Before cutover, we will make a check of...
If... are different, we will go back to...
Before I get..., I put... in a safe backup.
examples: Use take in, make a check, go back, and put for migration language.

sentences.text: The migration will take in active customers and seven years of payment records.
sentences.pattern: The migration will take in... and...
examples: The migration will take in open cases and their documents.
The migration will take in account data and payment history.

sentences.text: Before cutover, we will make a check of record counts and control totals.
sentences.pattern: Before cutover, we will make a check of... and...
examples: Before cutover, we will make a check of balances and sample records.
Before cutover, we will make a check of the backup and rollback steps.

sentences.text: If the numbers are different, we will go back to the old database.
sentences.pattern: If... are different, we will go back to...
examples: If the control totals are different, we will go back to the old system.
If the main test has an error, we will go back to the last safe point.

sentences.text: Before I get a new phone, I put my photos and contacts in a safe backup.
sentences.pattern: Before I get..., I put... in a safe backup.
examples: Before I get a new computer, I put my files in a safe backup.
Before I change my phone, I put my contact list in a safe backup.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Give a migration plan with scope, checks, and a way back, then add one personal backup example.

sentencePatterns: Let us make... clear: get... ready for...
We have capacity for..., so we will keep... out...
Before we take... in, we need...
I make a short list... so I do... first.
examples: Build a sprint commitment with make, get, keep, and take.

sentences.text: Let us make the sprint goal clear: get the payment check ready for SIT.
sentences.pattern: Let us make the sprint goal clear: get... ready for...
examples: Let us make the sprint goal clear: get the API ready for SIT.
Let us make the sprint goal clear: get the key UAT defects closed.

sentences.text: We have capacity for three stories, so we will keep the other work out of this sprint.
sentences.pattern: We have capacity for..., so we will keep... out of...
examples: We have capacity for two changes, so we will keep the report work out of this sprint.
We have capacity for the required scope, so we will keep the extra feature out.

sentences.text: Before we take a story in, we need clear acceptance criteria and no open dependency.
sentences.pattern: Before we take... in, we need... and...
examples: Before we take the API story in, we need sample data and a test endpoint.
Before we take the control story in, we need sign-off and a clear owner.

sentences.text: I make a short list before the weekend so I do the important things first.
sentences.pattern: I make a short list before... so I do... first.
examples: I make a short list before a journey so I do not leave important things at home.
I make a short list before shopping so I get the things I need first.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Make a sprint goal, set a capacity limit, and take in only ready work, then give one life-planning example.

sentencePatterns: This story has one purpose: keep... from...
We still have an open question about...
After we get..., we can give... and make it ready.
Before I make..., I take a look at...
examples: Use have, keep, get, give, make, and take to refine a story.

sentences.text: This story has one purpose: keep the same payment from going into the approval queue twice.
sentences.pattern: This story has one purpose: keep... from going into...
examples: This story has one purpose: keep an invalid account from going into payment.
This story has one purpose: keep an open error from going into production.

sentences.text: We still have an open question about a part match.
sentences.pattern: We still have an open question about...
examples: We still have an open question about the timeout rule.
We still have an open question about who may give approval.

sentences.text: After we get the examples, we can give the story a point value and make it ready.
sentences.pattern: After we get..., we can give... and make it ready.
examples: After we get the test data, we can give the story a point value.
After we get the API rules, we can make the story ready for planning.

sentences.text: Before I make an online order, I take a look at the size, price, and return rules.
sentences.pattern: Before I make..., I take a look at...
examples: Before I make a hotel booking, I take a look at the place and price.
Before I make a meal, I take a look at the food I have.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Give the story purpose, one open point, and what will make it ready, then add one life check.

sentencePatterns: This story is not ready because... may have...
We still need to get...
Let us keep it out... until...
I do not make... until I have...
examples: Use a small set of operator phrases to protect story quality.

sentences.text: This story is not ready because the business rules may have more than one meaning.
sentences.pattern: This story is not ready because... may have more than one meaning.
examples: This story is not ready because the error rule may have more than one meaning.
This story is not ready because the scope may have two different meanings.

sentences.text: We still need to get acceptance criteria, sample data, and a business owner.
sentences.pattern: We still need to get..., ..., and...
examples: We still need to get the API contract and a test endpoint.
We still need to get sign-off, an owner, and a target date.

sentences.text: Let us keep it out of sprint planning until every open point has an answer.
sentences.pattern: Let us keep it out of... until...
examples: Let us keep it out of the sprint until the dependency has a date.
Let us keep it out of planning until the business gives approval.

sentences.text: I do not make a travel booking until I have the date and price in writing.
sentences.pattern: I do not make... until I have...
examples: I do not make a large payment until I have the price in writing.
I do not make a dinner booking until I have the time and place.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Say why a story is not ready, what you need, and why it stays out, then give one careful life decision.

sentencePatterns: Both items have value, but... has...
If we put... first, we will have to put...
My suggestion is to take... first and keep... next.
When... are waiting, I do... first.
examples: Use have, put, take, keep, and do to make the trade-off clear.

sentences.text: Both items have value, but the regulatory change has a fixed date and greater business impact.
sentences.pattern: Both items have value, but... has...
examples: Both stories have value, but the control fix has greater business impact.
Both changes have value, but the client request has a fixed date.

sentences.text: If we put the report change first, we will have to put the onboarding change in the next sprint.
sentences.pattern: If we put... first, we will have to put... in...
examples: If we put the defect first, we will have to put the new feature in the next sprint.
If we put UAT support first, we will have to put the analysis work in next week.

sentences.text: My suggestion is to take the required work first and keep the other item next in line.
sentences.pattern: My suggestion is to take... first and keep... next in line.
examples: My suggestion is to take the control fix first and keep the report change next.
My suggestion is to take the client issue first and keep the system change next.

sentences.text: When two jobs at home are waiting, I do the one with the greater need first.
sentences.pattern: When... are waiting, I do... first.
examples: When two payments are waiting, I do the one with the earlier date first.
When two family needs are waiting, I do the more important one first.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Compare two items, put one first, and keep one next, then use the same rule for a life choice.

sentencePatterns: We may get to... if we have...
With the present scope, ... seems to be...
To get the earlier date, we have to make... or get...
If I have only..., I make... rather than...
examples: Make the date depend on clear conditions, not hope.

sentences.text: We may get to the end of November if we have sign-off this week.
sentences.pattern: We may get to... if we have...
examples: We may get to Friday if we have the test result by Wednesday.
We may get to the release date if we have the API on Monday.

sentences.text: With the present scope, 12 December seems to be the first safe target date.
sentences.pattern: With the present scope, ... seems to be the first safe target date.
examples: With the present defects, next Tuesday seems to be the first safe date.
With the present capacity, sprint 24 seems to be the first safe target.

sentences.text: To get the earlier date, we have to make the scope smaller or get more capacity.
sentences.pattern: To get the earlier date, we have to make... or get...
examples: To get the earlier date, we have to make UAT shorter or get more test help.
To get the earlier date, we have to make the release smaller or get another developer.

sentences.text: If I have only one hour, I make a simple meal rather than a complex one.
sentences.pattern: If I have only..., I make... rather than...
examples: If I have little time, I make a short journey rather than a long one.
If I have little money, I make a simple plan rather than an expensive one.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Give a possible date, a safe date, and the change needed for an earlier date, then add one life time choice.

sentencePatterns: We have... because of...
With this capacity, we can keep... but cannot take in...
We may get help from...
When I have little time, I put... first and let... wait.
examples: Use facts and simple operator phrases instead of pressure language.

sentences.text: We have two fewer developers because of leave and production support.
sentences.pattern: We have... fewer... because of...
examples: We have one fewer tester because of another release.
We have one BA this week because of planned leave.

sentences.text: With this capacity, we can keep the sprint goal but cannot take in more work.
sentences.pattern: With this capacity, we can keep... but cannot take in...
examples: With this capacity, we can keep the release date but cannot take in a new feature.
With this capacity, we can keep UAT support but cannot take in more analysis.

sentences.text: We may get help from the platform team for the API work.
sentences.pattern: We may get help from... for...
examples: We may get help from QA for the UAT work.
We may get help from the vendor for the migration work.

sentences.text: When I have little time, I put one important thing first and let the rest wait.
sentences.pattern: When I have little time, I put... first and let... wait.
examples: When I have little time, I put family needs first and let small jobs wait.
When I have little time, I put sleep first and let the housework wait.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Give the capacity fact, say what stays in, and ask for help, then add one life-capacity example.

sentencePatterns: I see why... wants... and why... wants...
We all have the same purpose...
Let us make a comparison of... with...
I let everyone give a reason before we make a choice.
examples: Lower the heat by seeing both sides and using the same points.

sentences.text: I see why the business wants a flexible rule and why Technology wants simple support.
sentences.pattern: I see why... wants... and why... wants...
examples: I see why Operations wants automation and why Risk wants a manual control.
I see why the vendor wants option one and why our team wants option two.

sentences.text: We all have the same purpose: a safe system that is simple to keep in operation.
sentences.pattern: We all have the same purpose: ...
examples: We all have the same purpose: a safe release with little customer impact.
We all have the same purpose: a clear process that is simple to support.

sentences.text: Let us make a comparison of both options with the same three points.
sentences.pattern: Let us make a comparison of... with the same...
examples: Let us make a comparison of both designs with cost, time, and risk.
Let us make a comparison of both dates with scope, capacity, and customer impact.

sentences.text: When my family has different ideas, I let everyone give a reason before we make a choice.
sentences.pattern: When... has different ideas, I let everyone give a reason before we make a choice.
examples: When friends have different ideas, I let everyone give a reason before we make a plan.
When we have different meal choices, I let everyone give an opinion first.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Show that you see both views, state the same purpose, and compare the options, then add one family example.

lessons.topic: Making a Decision in a Meeting
sentencePatterns: We have... options, and each one has...
I give... my support because...
If there is no strong argument against it, let us put...
I put the facts on paper and make...
examples: Close a choice with have, give, put, and make.

sentences.text: We have three options, and each one has a different balance of speed and control.
sentences.pattern: We have... options, and each one has a different balance of... and...
examples: We have two options, and each one has a different balance of cost and support.
We have three dates, and each one has a different balance of scope and risk.

sentences.text: I give option two my support because it keeps the control and the release date.
sentences.pattern: I give... my support because it keeps... and...
examples: I give the standard API my support because it keeps the design simple.
I give the smaller release my support because it keeps the target date safe.

sentences.text: If there is no strong argument against it, let us put this decision in the meeting record.
sentences.pattern: If there is no strong argument against it, let us put... in...
examples: If there is no strong argument against it, let us put the new date in the plan.
If there is no strong argument against it, let us put the owner in the action list.

sentences.text: When I have two good choices, I put the facts on paper and make one clear decision.
sentences.pattern: When I have... choices, I put... and make...
examples: When I have two travel choices, I put the price and time on paper.
When I have two job choices, I put the good and bad points on paper.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Set out the options, give one your support, and put the decision on record, then add one life decision.

sentencePatterns: The programme is on track, but...
The effect is limited to... and does not put...
We need... to give us support with...
When I give... an update, I say...
examples: Keep a management update short: status, effect, and ask.

sentences.text: The programme is on track, but one outside dependency needs attention.
sentences.pattern: The programme is on track, but... needs attention.
examples: UAT is on track, but one vendor item needs attention.
The release is on track, but final sign-off needs attention.

sentences.text: The effect is limited to the report work and does not put the main release at risk.
sentences.pattern: The effect is limited to... and does not put... at risk.
examples: The effect is limited to one market and does not put other regions at risk.
The effect is limited to test data and does not put production at risk.

sentences.text: We need this group to give us support with the vendor priority.
sentences.pattern: We need... to give us support with...
examples: We need this group to give us support with the scope decision.
We need management to give us support with short-term capacity.

sentences.text: When I give my family an update, I say what is going well, what is not, and what help I need.
sentences.pattern: When I give... an update, I say..., ..., and...
examples: When I give a friend an update, I say where I am and when I will come.
When I give my family a travel update, I say the time, place, and next step.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Give a management update with one message, one business effect, and one ask, then add one family update.

lessons.topic: Responding When You Don't Know the Answer
sentencePatterns: I do not have..., and I do not want to give...
I will make a check of... with...
I will send the answer... before...
If I do not have..., I get help rather than make a guess.
examples: Stay credible with have, give, make, and send.

sentences.text: I do not have that detail now, and I do not want to give a wrong answer.
sentences.pattern: I do not have..., and I do not want to give...
examples: I do not have the latest number now, and I do not want to give a wrong answer.
I do not have the contract detail now, and I do not want to give a guess.

sentences.text: I will make a check of the latest design with the solution architect.
sentences.pattern: I will make a check of... with...
examples: I will make a check of the defect list with QA.
I will make a check of the control rule with Compliance.

sentences.text: I will send the answer to everyone on this call before the end of the day.
sentences.pattern: I will send the answer to... before...
examples: I will send the answer to the project group before noon tomorrow.
I will send the answer to everyone after the vendor call.

sentences.text: If I do not have the answer, I get help rather than make a guess.
sentences.pattern: If I do not have..., I get help rather than make...
examples: If I do not have the right direction, I get help rather than make a guess.
If I do not have the full price, I get more information before I make a choice.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Say that you do not have the answer, give your check plan, and promise when you will send it, then add one life example.

sentencePatterns: What we see now is..., but...
Our first work is to get... and see...
We will give the next update at..., even if...
If... goes off, I keep calm and make a check of...
examples: Use only facts, the first action, and the next update time.

sentences.text: What we see now is that payments are late, but no payment is lost.
sentences.pattern: What we see now is that..., but...
examples: What we see now is that logins are slow, but current users are still in the system.
What we see now is that one region is down, but other markets are stable.

sentences.text: Our first work is to get the service back to a stable condition and see the customer effect.
sentences.pattern: Our first work is to get... and see...
examples: Our first work is to get payment processing back and see the queue size.
Our first work is to get access back and see how many users have an error.

sentences.text: We will give the next update at 2 p.m., even if we do not have the root cause.
sentences.pattern: We will give the next update at..., even if we do not have...
examples: We will give the next update in thirty minutes, even if we do not have a fix.
We will give the next update after the log check, even if we do not have full recovery.

sentences.text: If the power goes off at home, I keep calm and make a check of the main switch first.
sentences.pattern: If... goes off, I keep calm and make a check of... first.
examples: If my phone goes off, I keep calm and make a check of the battery first.
If the water goes off, I keep calm and make a check with the building manager.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Give the known facts, the first recovery action, and the next update time, then add one calm life response.

sentencePatterns: We have all key checks...
One... is still open, but we have...
My suggestion is to go ahead... and keep...
Before I go..., I make a check of...
examples: Base the release choice on evidence, remaining risk, and a clear suggestion.

sentences.pattern: We have all key checks: ..., ..., and...
examples: We have all key checks: business approval, smoke test, and support handover.
We have all key checks: data totals, access control, and rollback steps.

sentences.text: One medium defect is still open, but we have a tested workaround.
sentences.pattern: One... is still open, but we have...
examples: One report error is still open, but we have a manual workaround.

sentences.pattern: My suggestion is to go ahead with... and keep a close watch...
examples: My suggestion is to go ahead with cutover and keep a close watch on payment totals.
My suggestion is to go ahead as planned and keep a close watch on system use.

sentences.text: Before I go on a long journey, I make a check of my ticket, money, and phone.
sentences.pattern: Before I go..., I make a check of..., ..., and...
examples: Before I go to the airport, I make a check of my ticket and passport.
Before I go out for the day, I make a check of the weather and my phone.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Give the readiness evidence, one open risk, and your go/no-go suggestion, then add one personal readiness check.

sentencePatterns: Our work is dependent on... for...
To keep..., we have to get... by...
Let us put an owner, date, and path against...
If... is giving me..., I get... clear before...
examples: Make the handoff, date, and owner easy to see.

sentences.text: Our work is dependent on the upstream team for the final API contract and a stable test endpoint.
sentences.pattern: Our work is dependent on... for... and...
examples: Our work is dependent on Finance for the final accounting rules.
Our work is dependent on the downstream team for the final file format.

sentences.text: To keep our target date, we have to get both items by Wednesday.
sentences.pattern: To keep our target date, we have to get... by...
examples: To keep our target date, we have to get sign-off by Monday.
To keep our sprint goal, we have to get the test data before planning.

sentences.text: Let us put an owner, date, and escalation path against every open item.
sentences.pattern: Let us put an owner, date, and... against every...
examples: Let us put an owner and target date against every dependency.

sentences.text: If a friend is giving me a ride, I get the time and place clear before I go from home.
sentences.pattern: If... is giving me..., I get... clear before...
examples: If a friend is giving me help, I get the time and place clear first.
If someone is sending me a parcel, I get the delivery date clear first.

speakingChallenge.instruction: State the dependency, required date, and named action plan, then add one everyday dependency example.

sentencePatterns: We had an agreement to get... by...
Please give us... and...
We need a plan for making up...

sentences.pattern: We had an agreement to get... by...
examples: We had an agreement to get the estimate by noon today.
We had an agreement to get the test evidence before this meeting.

sentences.text: Please give us a confirmed date and a clear reason for the delay.
sentences.pattern: Please give us... and...
examples: Please give us the fix date and the reason for the error.
Please give us the support plan and the main contact name.

sentences.text: We also need a recovery plan for making up the lost time.
sentences.pattern: We also need a recovery plan for making up...
examples: We also need a recovery plan for making up the two-day delay.
We also need a recovery plan for keeping the new target date safe.

sentences.text: If an online order is late, I send the store the order number and make a request for a new date.
sentences.pattern: If... is late, I send... and make a request for...
examples: If a parcel is late, I send the store the receipt and make a request for help.
If a service is late, I send the company the details and make a request for a new time.

speakingChallenge.instruction: State the agreement, ask for a date and reason, and request a recovery plan, then add one life-service example.

sentencePatterns: One good point was getting...

Let us put... in one place and take a look at...
I make a note of one good thing and one change...
examples: Turn the review into one small action for the next sprint.

sentences.text: One good point was getting Operations into the story talks early.
sentences.pattern: One good point was getting... into... early.
examples: One good point was getting QA into the story talks early.
One good point was getting Risk into the design discussion early.

sentences.pattern: One trouble was that..., so... did not see...
examples: One trouble was that test data came late, so the team did not have enough time.

sentences.text: For the next sprint, let us put every decision in one place and take a look at it in stand-up.
sentences.pattern: For the next sprint, let us put... in one place and take a look at it...

sentences.text: At the end of the week, I make a note of one good thing and one change for next week.
sentences.pattern: At the end of..., I make a note of... and...
examples: At the end of the day, I make a note of one success and one open job.
At the end of a journey, I make a note of one good place and one useful change.

speakingChallenge.instruction: Give one good point, one trouble point, and one next-sprint change, then add one personal review habit.

sentencePatterns: Today we have three aims: see..., make..., and get...
I will take us through...

examples: Open with purpose and close with decisions, owners, and dates.

examples: Today we have three aims: see project status, make two decisions, and get clear owners.

sentences.pattern: I will take us through..., ..., and...
examples: I will take us through the business need, the options, and my suggestion.

examples: Before we go, I will give a short account of the scope and next steps.

sentences.pattern: When I make a plan with..., I put..., ..., and... in one message.
